page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-1200s-amd is a memory-optimized instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform, the system delivers 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache per core, alongside hardware support for cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI, as well as AVX vector processing.

Resource allocation is characterized by an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, totaling 192 GB of system memory. Bundled local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, providing low-latency disk access directly on the host node without reliance on network-attached storage. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Accelerated hardware such as dedicated GPUs is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute execution, placing in the top 25% for both stress-ng multi-core performance (67555.75) and Geekbench multi-core score (16500.0). Computational strengths extend to text processing, image processing, and CPU physics simulations. Memory subsystem throughput and standard operations demonstrate middle-tier results, reaching 141.36 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and sustaining 42.05 million Redis SET operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs center around instruction set capabilities and single-threaded limits. While dedicated cores ensure consistent execution without hypervisor noisy-neighbor interference, the AMD EPYC processor lacks AVX-512 extensions. In qualitative terms, the server provides high resource density for workloads demanding extensive RAM footprints and fast local disks without incurring the cost overhead of dedicated GPU coprocessors.

The configuration is suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency enterprise applications that benefit from a generous memory-to-core balance and direct NVMe storage throughput.

The high RAM allocation and fast local disk density make this configuration well matched for memory-resident databases, heavy caching layers, enterprise backend services, and transaction-heavy workloads.
